statement: SK Hynix is accelerating its 1c (sixth-generation 10nm-class) DRAM ramp to roughly 34% of its own DRAM production by Q4 2026 as it prepares for HBM4E.
why: The 1c node is the base die generation behind HBM4E, so how fast it ramps sets how quickly high-bandwidth memory supply for next-generation accelerators can grow.

impact.mechanism: A faster 1c node mix shift raises the bit supply and cost efficiency available for HBM4E, easing the memory input to next-generation GPU builds.

evidence.excerpt: with the process expected to account for roughly 34% of its DRAM production by the fourth quarter (Q4 2026), as the company prepares for HBM4E

confidence.basis: Secondary trade press, paywalled beyond the lede; no vendor disclosure read directly.

dispersion: The 34% figure is SK Hynix's own 1c-node share of its own DRAM production mix, not a market share and not a year-on-year bit-growth rate, so no measured value is recorded against the indicator's unit.
